rendered:
Cathode: the anode-free full cell uses pyrite (FeS2) as its cathode. The paper states that it "we employed pyrite (FeS2) for the cathode[1]" (see the schematic of the charged and discharged states in Fig. 4[2]).

Preparation: because pyrite natively contains no sodium, the cathode is presodiated before assembly: "presodiated the pyrite cathode prior to cell assembly[3]". The cells are built from this presodiated pyrite paired with carbon/Al current collectors, a discharged device state. On the initial charge, sodium ions leave the pyrite and are reduced on the carbon/Al collector to form sodium metal in situ, so the battery "does not contain sodium metal on assembly[4]".

Cathode capacity assumed for energy density: the energy density (∼400 Wh/kg[5]) is calculated from the mass of the presodiated pyrite, assuming a Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry and an FeS2 capacity of 335 mAh/g[6] (applied together with the carbon nucleation layer).
